common_name: Supertunia Latte Petunia (Silvery-White Petunia with Brown-Purple Veining)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated starts after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this is a trademarked Proven Winners selection sold only as rooted cuttings, not grown from seed.

directions: Supertunia Latte stood out among Proven Winners' spreading petunias for its unusual silvery-white petals overlaid with warm brown-to-purple veining, a muted, coffee-toned color that was a departure from the brighter pinks and purples typical of the Supertunia line. It carries the same vigorous, self-cleaning habit as other Supertunias, filling out quickly into a mounded, slightly trailing plant without any deadheading required through the season. Give it full sun and consistent moisture in containers, hanging baskets, or landscape beds, where its understated coloring reads as a sophisticated neutral alongside bolder companion plants. Pinch back leggy stems by a few inches in midsummer to encourage dense rebranching and a fresh flush of bloom into fall.

common_name: Supertunia Really Red Petunia (True Non-Fading Red Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated starts after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; this trademarked Proven Winners selection is sold as rooted cuttings rather than seed.

directions: Supertunia Really Red was bred to solve a long-standing weak point in red petunias, which have historically been prone to fading, bluing, or browning in intense heat; its blooms hold a clean, uniform true red from first flower to frost. The plant grows with the vigorous, slightly mounded and trailing habit typical of the Supertunia series, filling containers and landscape beds without any deadheading needed to sustain bloom. It performs best with full sun and even moisture, and benefits from a balanced liquid fertilizer every few weeks during peak summer growth to keep color saturated. Use it as a high-impact anchor color in patriotic, tropical, or monochrome red container combinations where fade resistance in the color red specifically is the priority.
sources: Proven Winners — Supertunia Really Red Petunia

common_name: Supertunia Mini Vista Scarlet Petunia (Compact Small-Flowered Scarlet-Red Spreading Petunia)
scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Supertunia Mini Vista Scarlet'

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated starts after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full to partial sun; space closer than full-size Supertunias to take advantage of this series' compact, small-flowered habit.

directions: Supertunia Mini Vista Scarlet brings the dense, heavily branched, small-flowered habit of the Mini Vista series to a vivid, true-red color, giving it a fuller flush of individual blooms than the larger-flowered Supertunia Vista line at a more restrained overall size. Its tighter growth habit fits smaller containers, window boxes, and tight landscape spots where a full-size spreading petunia would quickly outgrow its space. Like its series-mates it is self-cleaning and does not require deadheading, continuing to bloom from spring through frost with minimal upkeep. Grow it in full to part sun with regular moisture and a periodic feed to sustain the heavy bloom count the Mini Vista series is known for.
sources: Proven Winners — Supertunia Mini Vista Scarlet
Proven Winners — Supertunia Mini Vista Series

common_name: Supertunia Mini Vista Hot Pink Petunia (Compact Small-Flowered Hot Pink Spreading Petunia)
scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Supertunia Mini Vista Hot Pink'

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated starts after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full to partial sun; the Mini Vista series tolerates closer spacing than full-size Supertunias.

directions: Supertunia Mini Vista Hot Pink pairs the vivid, saturated magenta-pink color common to high-impact bedding petunias with the Mini Vista series' compact, densely branched, small-flowered form, so it reads as a solid carpet of color rather than a few large blooms scattered across foliage. It is well suited to mixed combination containers where its restrained size keeps it from overwhelming companion plants the way larger spreading Supertunias can. No deadheading is required to keep it flowering continuously from planting through the first hard frost. Provide full to part sun and consistent watering, and shear lightly in midsummer if growth becomes dense and tangled to refresh its shape.

common_name: Supertunia Mini Vista White Petunia (Compact Small-Flowered Pure White Spreading Petunia)
scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Supertunia Mini Vista White'

planting.note: Plant vegetatively propagated starts after all frost danger has passed in fertile, well-drained soil in full to partial sun; the compact Mini Vista habit suits smaller pots and tighter landscape spacing than full-size Supertunias.

directions: Supertunia Mini Vista White produces clean, bright white flowers in the same densely covered, small-flowered habit shared by the rest of the Mini Vista series, making it a workhorse filler for white-and-green combinations or moon gardens that read well at dusk. Its smaller overall footprint compared to full-size Supertunia Vista selections lets it fit snugly into mixed containers without crowding out neighboring plants. The plant is self-cleaning, dropping spent flowers on its own and needing no deadheading to maintain continuous bloom from spring to frost. Grow in full to part sun with even moisture, and watch for any green reversion shoots that occasionally appear in white-flowered petunias, removing them promptly to keep the display uniform.

common_name: Easy Wave Red Velour Petunia (Compact Mounding Velvety Blood-Red Spreading Petunia)
scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Easy Wave Red Velour'

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, or plant transplants after frost danger has passed, in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; space 10 to 12 inches apart for a dense bedding mass.

directions: Easy Wave Red Velour belongs to the Velour sub-group within the Easy Wave series, distinguished by a deeper, more saturated blood-red color with velvety-looking undertones and a darker throat than standard red petunias. It keeps the compact, mounding-yet-spreading habit the Easy Wave line is bred for, filling gaps quickly in beds and borders without sprawling as aggressively as the original Wave series. Being seed-raised, it germinates reliably from pelleted seed under warm conditions and grows on to flower heavily through summer with minimal pinching. Deadheading is not required, and a mid-season trim will refresh density if plants become stretched in high heat.
sources: Ball Seed — Easy Wave Red Velour Spreading Petunia

common_name: Easy Wave Plum Vein Petunia (Compact Mounding Lavender Petunia with Purple Veining)
scientific_name: Petunia x hybrida 'Easy Wave Plum Vein'

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, or plant transplants after frost danger has passed, in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; space 10 to 12 inches apart for a dense bedding mass.

directions: Easy Wave Plum Vein carries mid-lavender petals etched with darker plum-purple veining radiating out from the throat, a patterned look distinct from the solid colors found elsewhere in the Easy Wave lineup. Its compact, mounding growth habit spreads outward without the rangy sprawl of the original Wave series, making it easier to keep tidy in small beds, window boxes, and the front of mixed borders. Grown from pelleted seed, it establishes quickly under warm germination conditions and shifts from vegetative growth into heavy, self-cleaning bloom through the heat of summer. No deadheading is needed, though a light shearing in midsummer helps maintain a dense, well-branched habit if stems begin to thin.

common_name: Shock Wave Yellow Petunia (Small-Flowered True Yellow Spreading Petunia)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, or plant transplants after frost danger has passed, in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; space 10 to 12 inches apart for dense bedding or wider for a spreading groundcover effect.

directions: Shock Wave Yellow was a breeding milestone for PanAmerican Seed, bringing a genuinely clear yellow color into the small-flowered Shock Wave line after true yellow had long been difficult to achieve in spreading petunias without sacrificing vigor. It keeps the petite, abundant flower count and dense, mounding-spreading habit that defines the Shock Wave series, covering itself in blooms smaller than standard Wave or Easy Wave flowers but far more numerous. The plant tolerates heat and heavy summer rain well, continuing to rebound and rebloom without deadheading through the growing season. Pair it with the series' purple, denim, and ivory shades for high-contrast combination plantings, or let it stand alone as a bright groundcover in sunny beds and hanging baskets.
sources: PanAmerican Seed — Shock Wave Petunias Product Line
